assets.title: The handbook question that comes back every Monday
assets.content:
Subject: The handbook question that comes back every Monday
Preview text: The answer is already written down. orqAgent puts an agent over your documents and answers it in the channel.

Your handbook, answering questions in Slack

Hi there,

The same handbook questions come back to Slack every week. The answers are written down already — somebody still has to go and find them.

The usual route is keyword guesses and half-remembered page titles. Past a couple of hundred pages that stops landing, and every new hire starts over.

orqAgent is a no-code platform for building AI agents, and it is now available. You can put one agent over your own handbook documents and have it answer in the channel where the questions already arrive.

Upload PDFs, docs or plain text — the agent retrieves the most relevant context for every query, with no vector DB to manage. Slack connects by OAuth install, and the bot replies to mentions and channel messages.

If nobody at your company owns internal tooling, that is usually what stops a build like this. There is no backend of yours to host and no retrieval layer to maintain.

$0 to start — 1,500 free credits, no card required.

Point it at one set of policy documents and one channel. Whether the retrieval lands on the way your team words things is a question only your own handbook answers.

Create your first agent →

— the orqAgent team

P.S. Agent setup runs from the console — under two minutes to a first agent.

Profile-supported: the profile explicitly names Handbook/Docs/Issue Trackers as the target sources and Slack as the channel where repeat questions land, which the email's core scenario matches closely for Handbook and Notion docs. Gap: the profile also names Issue Trackers as a required source, and the email never mentions Issue Trackers at all, so the premise is only partially covered for someone whose actual ask includes that.
assumed_experiences: That the reader has already considered or been asked to build a Slack bot over the handbook and dreads owning the infrastructure (email-only, consistent with but not confirmed by profile's 'considering building')
That the reader's docs live in Notion or are uploadable files (profile-supported)
That the reader has personally fielded repeat policy questions by hand (profile-supported — profile states people ping this person directly)
That 'no vector DB to manage' and 'serverless' fully resolve the reliability/scale concerns of a production internal tool (email-only assertion, unverified)
reader_verdicts.problem_now: Documented as a current, ongoing pain in the supplied context (repeated policy questions, answers buried in hard-to-navigate docs) — not a hypothetical or scheduled event, so it reads as relevant to today, not just someday.
reader_verdicts.stopped_at: So people search by guessing document titles, and when that fails they ping a person.
reader_verdicts.biggest_doubt: This is an unknown vendor asking to ingest internal handbook/policy documents, and the email says nothing about where that data lives, who can see it, or any compliance posture — for someone standing this up for a whole company, that's the first question, and it isn't addressed. Also unclear how a 'no-code' single-agent, single-document-set demo scales to Handbook + Docs + Issue Trackers together, or what it costs past the free first agent.

Now available

Nobody wants to own another internal bot — this reads as disconnected header fragments before the greeting, unclear if it's a subhead, a section title, or stray preview text.
with no vector DB to manage — states the absence of a component without saying what actually happens to the data or who can see it, which is exactly the question a company-docs use case raises.

P.S. If you have already been asked to stand one up, this is the short version of that task. — vague callback that assumes context about a 'task' the email never actually described in full elsewhere, reads as filler.

Nobody wants to own another internal bot

Hi there,

Build a Slack bot over the handbook and you own it. Indefinitely.

That is usually where the idea stops. Meanwhile the same policy questions keep arriving in the channel, and the answers sit three sections deep in a page nobody thought to open.

So people search by guessing document titles, and when that fails they ping a person. The wiring that would fix it is the part that becomes yours: Slack events, a vector store, a model API, and whatever keeps them running next year.
